subject: english
question: Which of the following is a reason why remote workers are often more productive than those who work in a traditional office setting, according to the passage?

options.text: Remote workers have fewer distractions and interruptions.
Remote workers have access to better technology and equipment.
Remote workers have more opportunities for in-person collaboration.
Remote workers are given more autonomy and control over their work.

solution:
The correct answer is **"Remote workers have fewer distractions and interruptions."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage specifically mentions that one of the reasons remote workers tend to be more productive is due to reduced distractions and interruptions, which are common in a traditional office environment.
 
• Remote workers have the flexibility to create a personalized work environment that minimizes distractions and allows them to focus better on their tasks.
 
• Working remotely often enables employees to work during their most productive hours instead of being bound to a strict 9-to-5 schedule, which can further enhance productivity.
 
• Reduced time spent on commuting allows remote workers to dedicate more time and energy to their work tasks, contributing to higher productivity levels.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** "Option 1". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2 is incorrect because the passage does not mention access to better technology and equipment as a reason for increased productivity among remote workers.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect as the passage actually highlights a lack of in-person collaboration as a potential drawback of remote work, not a reason for increased productivity.
 
• Option 4 suggests that remote workers are given more autonomy and control over their work, and while this might contribute to a sense of job satisfaction, it is not explicitly mentioned in the passage as a reason for higher productivity.
